newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INTERVIEW-ESCO TO RESTRUCTURE ESTONIAN SHIPPING.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ESCO TO RESTRUCTURE ESTONIAN SHIPPING.

text.p: ESCO Holding, the winner of a bid to buy 70 percent of Estonian Shipping, said on Wednesday that its first plans were to restructure the company.
"The need to restructure is obvious," ESCO chairman Olev Schults told Reuters.
ESCO is held 50 percent by Norwegian Tschudi & Eitzen, 12 percent by Uhisinvesteeringud, Uhispank's investment arm, and 10 percent by U.S. Stanton Capital.
Estonian investment house Balti Cresco has 10 percent, the management of Estonian Shipping another 10 percent and eight percent belongs to EPEKS, an Estonian food production company.
"The Norwegian partner will guarantee that the best shipping know-how and experience is obtainable," Schults added.
Tschudi & Eitzen, established in 1883, has a fleet of ships worth a billion dollars. It has representatives in New York, Buenos Aires, Hong Kong and Copenhagen.
Schults said ESCO was hoping to turn the shipping company's loss of 76 million kroons in 1996 into profit this year.
"We are lucky with the decision and that our bid was preferred," he added.
ESCO made a 700 million kroon bid for the shipping company and has said it will invest 3.1 billion kroons, mostly in the modernisation of the shipping fleet.
Its business plan has two priorities: the first is the development of a highly competitive firm and the second to develop Estonia's transit trade.
ESCO plans to start operations with tankers.
It also wants to list the shipping company's shares on the bourses in Tallinn and Oslo.

Rival bidder Arbonale was formed by Talinvest and Hansa Investments, Estonian oil fuel terminal N-Terminaal, Norwegian shipper Navigator, investment bank Nomura and Hong Kong shipper Jinhui Shipping and Transportation Ltd .
Arbonale bid 612 million kroons and wanted to invest 3.55 billion kroons in the company.
